options: a:One drink can affect your driving.,b:Two drinks are required before impairment.,c:Three drinks are needed to affect you.
note: Even a single alcoholic drink can impair judgment and reaction time; it's unsafe to drive after drinking any amount.

question: If another vehicle cuts in front of you dangerously close, what is the best immediate action?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas to increase space.,b:Honk and brake hard.,c:Swerve into the adjacent lane suddenly.
note: Removing your foot from the accelerator slows you and increases space without abrupt braking or risky maneuvers.

question: To reduce the chance of hydroplaning during rain, you should:
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Put on cruise control to maintain speed.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts raining.
note: Lower your speed in wet conditions to reduce the risk of tires losing contact with the road surface and hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:When traffic on the street you are turning onto moves to the left.,b:If you increase your speed before the turn.,c:Only if traffic moves to the right on the street you're entering.
note: You may turn left from a one-way onto another one-way street only if traffic on that street moves to the left and no sign forbids it.

question: When a red light is displayed but a green arrow points the way, when may you proceed?
options: a:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop first.,c:Only after the red light changes to green.
note: A green arrow authorizes movement in the arrow's direction if you're in the correct lane, but you must still yield to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, how should you respond?
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children.,b:Always stop even if no stop sign is present.,c:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,d:Increase speed to clear the crossing quickly.
note: Pentagonal signs warn of a school zone or school crossing—be alert for children and ready to stop.

question: If another driver is passing you in a no-passing zone, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position to allow the other driver to re-enter safely.,b:Pull off the road to make more room.,c:Brake abruptly to prevent the pass.,d:Speed up to prevent being passed.
note: If you are being passed illegally in a no-passing zone, maintain steady speed and position so the passing driver can return to the lane safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On or near any curve or hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a straight roadway with clear visibility for 500 feet both ways.
note: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see oncoming traffic; it creates a serious collision risk.

question: If bad weather reduces visibility, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
note: When visibility is poor, increase the gap between you and the vehicle ahead to allow more reaction time.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what action should you take?
options: a:Slow down gradually and avoid braking.,b:Apply the brakes firmly to regain traction.,c:Maintain speed to drive through the water quickly.
note: If hydroplaning occurs, ease off the accelerator and allow the vehicle to slow; do not brake hard, which can worsen the loss of control.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Farther behind the truck than you would follow a passenger vehicle.,b:Closer behind the truck than behind a passenger vehicle.,c:Directly to the right of the truck at all times.,d:In the truck's blind spot to improve aerodynamics.
note: Trucks have larger blind spots and longer stopping distances; maintain extra following distance when behind them.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers only.
note: Low beams (and fog lights if equipped) improve visibility in fog; high beams cause glare and reduced visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Whenever a police officer orders you to stop or at a red traffic light.,b:Only at a red light but not for officers.,c:Only when directed by traffic signs and not officers.,d:When another driver waves you down.
note: You must obey police officers directing traffic at all times and stop at red lights; their instructions override signals and signs.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should:
options: a:Allow extra space in front of your vehicle.,b:Follow at the same distance as for passenger cars.,c:Follow more closely so you can see around it.
note: Give motorcycles extra room; they can stop more quickly and are harder to see, especially at night due to a single tail light.

question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:You may proceed through the intersection at a safe, reasonable speed if it is clear.,b:Increase your speed to clear the intersection immediately.,c:Adjust your mirrors then proceed.
note: A steady green light means you may go, but you must yield to pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection and proceed only when safe.

question: Like alcohol and drugs, what effect can drowsiness have on driving?
options: a:Impair your judgment.,b:Help you become more alert.,c:Improve reaction time.,d:Have no effect at all.
note: Drowsiness reduces alertness, slows reactions, and impairs judgment, increasing crash risk.

question: When is hand-over-hand steering the recommended technique?
options: a:When making sharp turns at low speed.,b:When backing up or briefly turning for wipers or radio.,c:During normal, gentle lane changes at highway speed.
note: Hand-over-hand steering is appropriate for sharp turns; for small steering adjustments or backing, other methods are used.

question: After a minor, non-injury intersection collision with little damage, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane.,b:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.,c:Never move your vehicle under any circumstances.
note: If there are no injuries and the vehicle can be moved safely, move it out of traffic to prevent secondary crashes and clear the roadway.

question: If you must park where parking is not normally provided, what should you ensure?
options: a:Make the vehicle visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,b:Park with your reverse lights on.,c:Park five feet from the curb.,d:Leave the engine running.
note: When parking in an unusual spot, make sure your vehicle does not become a hazard and is visible to approaching traffic.

question: How should you behave when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Pass carefully and avoid slowing to look at the work.,b:Stop to watch the workers.,c:Decrease your following distance to clear the zone faster.
note: Drive cautiously through work zones and avoid “rubbernecking” (slowing to look), which adds to congestion and danger.

question: A driver license is considered which of the following?
options: a:A privilege that can be revoked.,b:A guaranteed civil right.,c:A mandatory possession for all citizens.
note: A driver license is a privilege granted by the state that can be suspended or revoked for violations; it is not an absolute right.

question: If a vehicle is about to hit you from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Brace yourself by pressing your back and head against the seat and head restraint.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to apply brakes.
note: If hit from behind, keep your seat belt fastened and brace against the seat and head restraint to reduce whiplash; maintain a firm grip on the wheel and be prepared to brake.

question: Before changing lanes or passing, what steps should you take?
options: a:Check mirrors, check blind spots, and signal your intention.,b:Signal only after you start to move into the other lane.,c:Rely solely on your mirrors and omit a head check.,d:Honk to warn drivers instead of signaling.
note: Always check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, and signal before changing lanes or passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right, which path should you steer?
options: a:A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,b:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,c:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,d:Directly onto the shoulder.
note: Steer a middle course to maximize clearance from both oncoming traffic and hazards from parked vehicles.

question: How does a BAC of 0.02 percent affect accident risk?
options: a:It nearly doubles the driver’s chance of a crash.,b:It has no effect on driving ability.,c:It only affects drivers under 21.,d:It makes you immune to impairment.
note: Even small increases in BAC significantly increase the risk of being in a fatal crash; impairment begins at low levels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should the maximum posted speed limit be driven?
options: a:Under ideal conditions.,b:Only during the day.,c:Only during the night.
note: The maximum posted speed is appropriate only under ideal driving, road, and weather conditions; adjust speed downward when conditions warrant.

question: When changing lanes, what should you do to check for traffic in your blind spot?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,c:Rely only on the left side mirror.,d:Sound your horn before moving.
note: A shoulder check helps you notice vehicles in blind spots that mirrors may not reveal before a lane change.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always look:
options: a:To the left and right sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,b:Only ahead and rely on signals.,c:Only behind you to check for following traffic.
note: At places where people or vehicles may enter your path, look left and right to be sure no one is approaching before proceeding.

question: Which road surface is most likely to be icy after snow or rain on cold days?
options: a:Roads in shaded areas.,b:Open hilly roads.,c:Residential streets that get sun.,d:Major highways with traffic.
note: Shaded portions of the roadway freeze and thaw more slowly, making them more likely to be icy than open areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Follow the officer's direction and go through the intersection.,b:Stop until the light turns green.,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,d:Ignore the officer and obey the traffic signal.
note: Officers directing traffic override traffic signals; follow their instructions for safety and legal compliance.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the bloodstream can impair a driver's:
options: a:Right-of-way privileges.,b:Knowledge only.,c:Judgment and physical coordination.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can reduce judgment and coordination and increase the risk of criminal charges if you drive impaired.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you begin driving.,b:Only when you need them while driving.,c:After you start moving the vehicle.
note: Adjust mirrors, your seat, and fasten your safety belt before you start driving for safety and minimal distraction.

question: When is highway pavement most slippery after rain begins?
options: a:Right when it first starts to rain.,b:After it has been raining several hours.,c:One to two hours after it starts raining.
note: Roads are especially slippery when rain first starts because oils and deposits on the surface create a greasy film until washed away.

question: Because motorcycles and scooters are harder to see, you should:
options: a:Make constant visual checks and be especially alert.,b:Share a lane with the motorcycle.,c:Slow only when behind them.
note: Motorcycles and mopeds are easily hidden in blind spots; make frequent visual checks and give them full lane space.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its signal arm extended, you must:
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the bus resumes motion and signals are retracted.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are visible.,c:Proceed at normal speed but watch for children.
note: You must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing lights and extended arm until all signals are cleared, regardless of your direction of travel.

question: When a centerline consists of double solid yellow lines, what is the passing rule?
options: a:No passing from either direction.,b:Passing permitted from the left only.,c:Passing permitted from the right only.,d:Passing permitted if no oncoming traffic.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate that passing is prohibited in both directions because traffic moves in opposite directions and visibility is limited.

question: When changing lanes, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Changing lanes abruptly or without signaling.,b:Looking over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Checking for other vehicles that may move into the same lane.,d:Using your turn signal to alert others.
note: Never change lanes suddenly or without signaling; check mirrors and blind spots to ensure the lane is clear.

question: In foggy conditions, what is the proper driving action?
options: a:Slow down and use low beam headlights.,b:Turn on high beam headlights to cut through the fog.,c:Increase speed to get through the fog faster.,d:Turn on interior dome lights.
note: Slow your speed and use low beams; if visibility is extremely poor, pull safely off the road and wait for conditions to improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection where all corners have stop signs, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived before you.,b:The driver on your left.,c:The driver across from your vehicle.
note: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order of arrival; if multiple vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: If you see heavy smoke covering the roadway ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,b:Turn on your four-way flashers and proceed.,c:Turn on your high beams and continue driving.
note: Reduce speed, pull as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway until it's safe to proceed when smoke obscures the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When your view of cross traffic at an intersection is blocked, how should you proceed?
options: a:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly both ways.,b:Slow down briefly and look both directions without stopping.,c:Keep your speed and look both ways.
note: If your view is obscured, come to a stop and move forward slowly until you have a clear view of the cross traffic before entering.

question: What do 'No passing zone' signs indicate to drivers?
options: a:That it is unsafe and illegal to pass in the marked area.,b:To slightly increase your speed.,c:To maintain a steady speed only.
note: A 'No passing zone' indicates you must not attempt to pass another vehicle because visibility or road conditions make it unsafe.

question: What should you do with loose objects inside your vehicle?
options: a:Secure them so they won’t become hazards in a sudden stop.,b:Place them on the dashboard for easy access.,c:Leave them on the floor near the driver’s seat.,d:Put them in the passenger seat to watch over them.
note: Loose items can fly and injure occupants or interfere with controls; secure cargo and items before driving.

question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:
options: a:The yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,b:The opposite side has a broken yellow line.,c:The vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.,d:The road is clear for 100 feet ahead.
note: Crossing double lines is allowed only if the line on your side is dashed (broken), indicating permitted passing.

question: How dangerous is backing your vehicle?
options: a:Always dangerous.,b:Only dangerous in large vehicles.,c:Dangerous only if you have a helper guiding you.
note: Backing is always hazardous because visibility is limited; use extra caution and helpers when appropriate.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.,b:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road away from traffic.,c:Signal and move into the slow lane.,d:Keep driving until you find a service station.
note: If possible, get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic, and turn on emergency flashers so other drivers can see that you have a problem.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and enter the interstate only after identifying a gap in traffic.,b:Immediately enter the far-right lane and then speed up.,c:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to speed.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a police signal.
note: On short ramps without an acceleration lane, wait for a safe gap and then accelerate to merge; do not enter until safe.

question: What does a steady red arrow pointing right mean at an intersection?
options: a:You must stop and may not turn in that direction until the signal changes.,b:You may turn after slowing and yielding to traffic.,c:You may turn after making a complete stop.,d:You may turn only if no pedestrians are present.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and are not allowed to turn in that direction until a green signal permits it.

question: How can sudden wind gusts on highways affect drivers?
options: a:They can cause problems for all vehicles, not just large ones.,b:They only affect large vehicles.,c:They only cause visibility problems.
note: Strong wind can reduce visibility by blowing debris and can physically affect the stability of many types of vehicles, not only large ones.

question: If a child is bicycling near your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Expect the unexpected and be prepared for sudden moves.,b:Beep your horn to get their attention.,c:Assume the child is in total control of the bicycle.
note: Children on bicycles are unpredictable; slow down and be ready for sudden direction changes or stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:When there is a broken yellow line next to your lane and it is safe to pass.,b:When you are on a hill or curve with good visibility.,c:When a solid line is next to your driving lane.,d:At a railroad crossing.
note: A broken yellow line beside your lane indicates you may pass when it's safe; solid lines or poor visibility prohibit passing.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and yield only if necessary.,c:Wait for the light to turn green before moving.,d:Proceed without stopping if no one else is present.
note: A flashing red traffic signal is treated like a stop sign: stop fully, yield, and proceed when clear.

question: Large trucks are most likely to lose speed when:
options: a:Driving up long or steep hills.,b:Driving down long gradual hills.,c:Driving in long, gradual curves.
note: Trucks take longer to accelerate and often slow when climbing long or steep inclines; give them extra space on hills.

question: If a tire blows out, what immediate action should you take?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow gradually, using brakes lightly.,b:Apply the brake and hold it hard.,c:Pull over immediately without slowing gradually.
note: Keep the vehicle straight, ease off the accelerator, and slow gradually using light braking if necessary; then pull off the road when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and not already in the intersection, you should:
options: a:Stop safely if you can do so.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Proceed without slowing.,d:Ignore the signal and follow the vehicle ahead.
note: A steady yellow warns the light will soon turn red; stop safely if you can, otherwise clear the intersection carefully.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After completing a pass, when is it safe to return to your driving lane?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:After signaling for at least three seconds.,c:When the other driver signals you to return to the lane.
note: Only return to your driving lane when you can clearly see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, indicating enough space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your original lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After you have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.,d:When the passed vehicle signals you to return.
note: Only move back when you can clearly see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your mirror and it is safe to do so.

question: At a railroad crossing you must:
options: a:Watch for vehicles required to stop at all railroad crossings and for multiple trains.,b:Only look for a single train approaching.,c:Proceed without stopping if you don't see a train immediately.,d:Drive faster to clear the tracks quickly.
note: Approach crossings cautiously; be aware some vehicles must always stop at crossings and multiple trains may pass on different tracks.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and immediately.,b:Slow down gradually and use the brakes lightly.,c:Pump the brakes to slow quickly.
note: Ease off the accelerator, steer straight, and slow gradually; do not brake hard until the vehicle has slowed considerably.

question: Before you enter an intersection, where should you look?
options: a:Left, then right, then left again.,b:Only to the left once.,c:Only to the right.,d:Down at the instrument panel.
note: Check both directions before entering an intersection; look left again because vehicles from that side are closer.

question: Why should drivers give children on bicycles extra space?
options: a:They are smaller, harder to see, and have less reliable reflexes than adults.,b:They drive faster than adults.,c:They always use bike lanes correctly.
note: Children are less predictable, smaller, and have slower decision-making and reflexes, so allow extra space and caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic you should do what first?
options: a:Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead and the gap.,b:Only watch the vehicle ahead of the gap.,c:Speed up and force other vehicles to make room.
note: Before merging or changing lanes, check behind and to the sides as well as the vehicles ahead to ensure the gap is safe to enter.

question: What must drivers do when a school bus is loading or unloading children?
options: a:Come to a complete stop regardless of your direction of travel.,b:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus.,c:Slow down and be ready to stop but not necessarily stop.,d:Pass the bus cautiously if no children are crossing.
note: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off passengers, all approaching drivers from either direction must stop until children are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive slower than the normal flow of traffic, you will most likely:
options: a:Interfere with traffic and possibly receive a ticket.,b:Improve traffic flow.,c:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving significantly below the flow of traffic can impede normal movement and may lead to a citation; match traffic speed within limits.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires you to:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped while it flashes.,d:Proceed as if it were a flashing yellow light.
note: Treat a flashing red signal like a stop sign: stop, yield to others, and only proceed when the way is clear.

question: In heavy fog, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Emergency flashers only.
note: Use low beams (and fog lights if equipped) in fog, rain, or snow; high beams cause reflection and reduce visibility.

question: Which foot should you use for both the brake and accelerator?
options: a:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.,b:Use your left foot to brake.,c:Always brake abruptly to stop quickly.
note: Use your right foot for accelerator and brake; brake smoothly with increasing pressure for a controlled stop.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using its flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.,b:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling over to the right edge of the road and stopping until they have passed.

question: If a pedestrian with a guide dog is at a corner ready to cross before you make a right turn, what must you do?
options: a:Wait until the person has crossed before turning.,b:Tell the pedestrian when it is safe to cross.,c:Turn off your engine until they finish crossing.,d:Proceed if you think you can beat them across.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must be given the right-of-way; wait until they have crossed before turning.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Traffic next to the broken line may pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.,b:Passing is prohibited in both directions.,c:Passing is permitted only from the lane next to the solid line.,d:Passing is permitted in both directions.
note: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line allows passing from the side with the broken line but prohibits passing from the side with the solid line.

question: Why is driving at night generally more hazardous than daytime driving?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is always slower at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night and glare from headlights limit how far ahead you can see, making night driving inherently more risky.

question: When you see pedestrians near the roadway, how should you respond?
options: a:Slow down and pass with caution.,b:Sound your horn and maintain speed.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: Slow down and be prepared to stop; pedestrians near the road may step into your path unexpectedly.

question: If you want to enter a freeway but there is no gap in traffic, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap so you can accelerate to traffic speed.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp until traffic clears.,c:Force other drivers to make space by maintaining ramp speed.
note: If you cannot find a gap, reduce speed on the ramp and wait for a safe opening rather than stopping at the ramp end or forcing entry.

question: When a school bus on your side of the road has its red lights flashing, what is required of you?
options: a:Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.,b:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,c:Stop until the lights stop flashing.,d:Proceed once the students have moved away from the bus.
note: The bus's flashing red lights and stop arm mean you may not proceed until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted.

question: How close to a fire hydrant are you prohibited from parking?
options: a:Within 15 feet.,b:Within 20 feet.,c:Within 30 feet.
note: You must not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant so emergency services can access it quickly.

question: How should you check your vehicle's blind spots?
options: a:By turning your head and glancing over your shoulder.,b:By looking only in your side mirrors.,c:By checking only your rearview mirror.,d:By relying on rear sensors only.
note: Blind spots cannot be fully seen with mirrors alone; glance over your shoulder to check those areas before changing lanes or merging.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights, where should you briefly look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:Stare at the centerline of the road.,c:Flash your high beams to warn the other driver.
note: Glance briefly toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights, then resume scanning ahead.

question: When parallel parked facing downhill, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels sharply toward the side of the road (toward the curb).,b:Turn the wheels away from the side of the road.,c:Keep the wheels straight.,d:Turn the wheels to the left only.
note: When parking downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if the brakes fail.

question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from a driveway or alley, what should a driver do?
options: a:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area.,b:Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield.,c:Stop only if pedestrians are present.,d:Honk to warn pedestrians.
note: You must stop before entering the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians; they have the right-of-way when you cross a sidewalk.

question: Which part of driving does alcohol affect first?
options: a:Judgment and decision-making.,b:Vision before anything else.,c:Balance before mental skills.,d:Only coordination initially.
note: Alcohol impacts judgment and reasoning before it affects other skills, making poor decisions more likely early on.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and the driver on your left arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, who goes first?
options: a:The driver on your right has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:The driver signaling a turn has the right-of-way.
note: When vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: Where should a driver direct their attention while driving?
options: a:Scan ahead, to the sides, and to the rear of the vehicle.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Focus only on the middle of the road.,d:Look only at the instrument panel.
note: A safe driver constantly scans ahead, to the sides, and behind to be aware of hazards and traffic around the vehicle.

question: At about what speed can a car begin to hydroplane on wet pavement?
options: a:Around 35 miles per hour.,b:Around 45 miles per hour.,c:Around 40 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can start at speeds near 35 mph as tires lose the ability to channel water away and may ride on top of the water.

question: Before stopping at a traffic light or sign, what should you do first?
options: a:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,b:Set the parking brake.,c:Press down hard on the accelerator.
note: Before stopping, check mirrors for traffic behind and around you so you can slow smoothly and safely.

question: When descending a long or steep hill, what should you do regarding vehicles behind you?
options: a:Check your mirrors often for fast-approaching vehicles.,b:Assume traffic behind you keeps a constant speed.,c:Hold the brake pedal down steadily to control speed.
note: Vehicles can gain speed going downhill; frequently check mirrors so you are aware of faster traffic approaching from behind.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,b:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.,c:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,d:Herbal supplements never affect driving ability.
note: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair driving; it is illegal to drive while impaired by any substance.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means passing is:
options: a:Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.,b:Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,c:Not permitted from either side.,d:Allowed only during daylight.
note: If the broken line is on your side, you may pass when it is safe; if the solid is on your side, passing is prohibited.

question: What is the safe condition to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you can see the other vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:When you have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.,c:When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,d:When you feel comfortable.
note: Only return to your lane after passing when you can clearly see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: How must you respond to a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Come to a full stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and go through if no cars are visible.,c:Wait for the light to turn green before proceeding.,d:Stop only if other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: stop fully, yield, and proceed when clear.

question: What does an orange-and-red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle indicate?
options: a:The vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle.,b:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:The vehicle is an emergency vehicle.,d:The vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
note: Slow-moving vehicles such as tractors or road maintenance equipment display an orange-red triangle to warn following traffic.

question: What is the safest method for changing from one lane to another?
options: a:Change lanes quickly and often.,b:Only change lanes when another car is in your blind spot.,c:Change lanes gradually and carefully.,d:Always avoid changing lanes.
note: Always change lanes gradually and carefully; unnecessary lane changes increase the risk of accidents.

question: How should head restraints be positioned for maximum safety?
options: a:Adjusted to contact the back of the occupant’s head.,b:Removed if they feel uncomfortable.,c:Set as low as possible behind the seat.,d:Folded down when not in use.
note: Head restraints should contact the back of the head to help prevent whiplash in rear-end collisions.

question: If you experience a sudden tire blowout, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly and ease off the gas, then brake gently.,b:Pump the brakes repeatedly to slow down.,c:Apply the brakes as hard as possible immediately.,d:Turn the steering wheel sharply toward the shoulder.
note: With a blowout, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas, and brake gently to slow before pulling off safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving at high speeds, how long before changing lanes or turning should you signal?
options: a:Four to five seconds.,b:Two seconds.,c:Ten seconds.,d:One second.
note: At higher speeds you should signal earlier—about four to five seconds before making the maneuver—to give other drivers time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is not operating, how should you treat the intersection?
options: a:As an all-way stop; stop and yield before entering.,b:You may proceed if the intersection appears clear.,c:Drive quickly through to clear the intersection.,d:Obey only the stop lines and not other vehicles.
note: When signals are out, treat the intersection like an all-way stop: come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before going.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway from a ramp, you should:
options: a:Check for cars, increase speed to match traffic, and merge when clear.,b:Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.,c:Check for cars and reduce speed to 25 mph before entering the lane.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speed, check for a safe gap, and merge smoothly into traffic.

question: After passing on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:After about three seconds have passed.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,d:As soon as you finish accelerating.
note: You may return to the right lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, indicating you have enough room.

question: Which headlights should be used when driving in fog, rain, or snow?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Fog lights only without beams.,d:Parking lights only.
note: Low beams reduce reflection and glare in fog, rain, or snow. High beams will reflect and impair visibility.

question: Which driving abilities are diminished by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination.,b:Only alertness and concentration.,c:Only reaction time and coordination.,d:None; only vision is affected.
note: Alcohol and many drugs reduce alertness and concentration and increase reaction time while reducing coordination — all vital driving skills.

question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:If there isn't room on the other side for you to fully clear the tracks.,b:Only when the crossing is in a city or town.,c:Only if you are transporting two or more young children.
note: Never stop on the tracks; if you cannot fully clear them due to traffic or obstacles, wait until the way is clear before crossing.

question: Give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:
options: a:Crossing any street (in marked or unmarked crosswalks).,b:Only in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only in any crosswalk or intersection.,d:Wearing bright clothing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks and should exercise caution for anyone crossing a street.

question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.,d:Interior lights for better visibility.
note: Low beams reduce glare from reflections; high beams will reflect off the fog and worsen visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, how can you check your blind spot?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder into the lane you intend to enter.,b:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Use only the side mirror.
note: Always look over your shoulder to check the blind spot in the direction of the lane change in addition to checking mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, what speed should you aim for?
options: a:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.,b:More slowly than freeway traffic.,c:At the legal speed limit regardless of traffic speed.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic and merge smoothly; do not stop unless no gap exists.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop immediately.,c:Stop and proceed only when no vehicles are present.
note: A flashing yellow means slow down and proceed with caution; you do not have to stop if the way is clear.

question: When driving at night, you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Look directly at oncoming headlights to adjust.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance and use proper headlight settings to improve safety.

question: Having a driver license is considered a:
options: a:Privilege.,b:Requirement.,c:Right.,d:Public entitlement.
note: Driving is a privilege granted by the state that can be suspended or revoked for misuse or violations.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding posted speeds or driving too fast for conditions.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Scanning the environment regularly.,d:Obeying traffic laws.
note: Driving above posted speeds or too fast for conditions is a leading factor in many crashes; safe driving matches conditions and the flow of traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a curbside parked position, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for a large enough gap so you can accelerate up to traffic speed before merging.,b:Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,c:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass then enter in front of them.
note: Only enter traffic when there is a gap large enough for you to reach the flow speed and merge safely; do not dawdle.

question: What is a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.,c:Anything that causes evasive action only.
note: A distraction is any activity or object that diverts attention from driving and can lead to crashes.

question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light before moving.,c:Increase your speed to clear the intersection quickly.,d:Ignore it unless pedestrians are present.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down, be alert, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a green light but the intersection is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Do not enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,b:Partially enter the intersection to hold your right-of-way.,c:Enter and wait for traffic to clear while blocking the crosswalk.
note: Never enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking an intersection is illegal and dangerous.

question: How does driving on gravel or dirt roads affect traction and stopping?
options: a:Stopping distance is shorter.,b:Tires have less traction on gravel and dirt so you must slow down.,c:Tires grip the road better than on pavement.,d:Visibility is better than on pavement.
note: Loose gravel and dirt reduce tire traction compared to pavement; you must slow down because it takes longer to stop and skids are more likely.

question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle with ABS, what is the correct braking method?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes manually.,c:Stay off the brakes and let the vehicle drift to a stop.
note: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems require firm continuous pressure on the brake pedal; the system pulses the brakes automatically.

question: What is the best general method to avoid dangerous driving situations?
options: a:Be aware of everything happening around your vehicle.,b:Turn off the radio to eliminate distractions.,c:Keep your gaze fixed directly ahead at all times.
note: Constantly scanning front, sides, and rear allows you to spot hazards early and take appropriate action to avoid them.

question: If a road is slippery, what following distance should you keep?
options: a:Farther from the car ahead than normal.,b:No different than normal.,c:Closer to the car ahead than normal.
note: Increase following distance on slippery roads because you need more space to stop safely.

question: How can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning in heavy rain?
options: a:Slow down and drive at a reduced speed for conditions.,b:Apply brakes hard as soon as the vehicle begins to skid.,c:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of rain.,d:Turn off your ABS system to improve traction.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose contact with the road; slowing down in wet conditions reduces that risk.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to an officer?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:If stopped for a citation or involved in a collision.,c:Only when stopped and cited.
note: You must carry evidence of financial responsibility (insurance) and present it to a law enforcement officer after a traffic stop or collision.

question: Traffic control devices used in construction and maintenance areas are what color?
options: a:Orange.,b:Red.,c:Yellow.,d:Blue.
note: Orange is the designated color for construction and maintenance warnings; exercise extra caution in these zones.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, which lane position may they legally use?
options: a:They may use the left lane when turning left.,b:They may cut through all lanes at once.,c:They must always wait on the side of the road.
note: Bicyclists may take the leftmost lane or otherwise use traffic lanes to complete left turns safely, similar to motor vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must drivers be prepared to do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic close enough to cause conflict.,b:Yield only to vehicles on the right.,c:Slow but never stop.
note: At a yield sign you must be prepared to stop and give right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Both to any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists, and to vehicles already in the roundabout.,b:Only to vehicles already in the roundabout.,c:Only to pedestrians and bicyclists.
note: When entering a roundabout you must yield to pedestrians/bicyclists crossing and to traffic already circulating within the roundabout.

question: Which substances can impair your driving ability?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, and certain cough/cold medicines.,b:Only illegal drugs, not prescription medications.,c:Only alcohol and narcotics, not over-the-counter remedies.,d:Vitamins and herbal teas exclusively.
note: Many prescription, illegal, and over-the-counter drugs (including those with codeine or antihistamines) can impair driving skills.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If several vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The largest vehicle goes first.,d:The driver turning left proceeds first.
note: At uncontrolled intersections, drivers yield to vehicles on their right when arriving at the same time.

question: If a vehicle has a two-part seat belt system, how should it be used?
options: a:Wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt together.,b:Use only the lap belt for comfort.,c:Use the shoulder belt alone without the lap belt.,d:Remove the shoulder portion if it’s uncomfortable.
note: Both lap and shoulder belts must be worn together for proper protection; using one part alone greatly reduces safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are continuously being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the lane on your right.,b:Stay in the center lane.,c:Move to the lane on your left.,d:Slow to the minimum speed limit.
note: On multi-lane highways, stay in the right lanes unless passing or preparing for a left turn; if traffic passes frequently on both sides, move right when safe.

question: If a school bus ahead in your lane is stopped with red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped while the red lights are flashing.,b:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Stop only until you believe all children have exited the bus.,d:Proceed if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.
note: When a stopped school bus uses flashing red lights you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing; you do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

question: How must you respond when a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane is crossing the street?
options: a:Always yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,b:Tell them the safest path to cross.,c:Proceed if they wait for you to pass.,d:Honking is permitted to speed them up.
note: Blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog always have the right-of-way and must be yielded to.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.,b:The light is about to turn green so prepare to go.,c:The same as a yield sign — slow and yield.,d:Proceed without stopping if no cars are visible.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, then proceeding when safe.

question: Blue traffic signs provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food, etc.).,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Mileage information and distances.,d:Regulatory instructions.
note: Blue signs are service signs that inform drivers of nearby facilities and services such as gas, food, or hospitals.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:Alcohol impairs judgment, which is essential for safe driving.,b:If you can walk in a straight line, it is safe to drive.,c:Being under the legal BAC limit means you are not impaired.,d:Alcohol only affects coordination, not decision-making.
note: Alcohol reduces judgment and decision-making ability, which are crucial for safe driving; impairment can occur even below legal BAC limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Activate your turn signal.,c:Brake hard while turning.,d:Increase your speed to maintain momentum.
note: Slow down before entering a curve to maintain control and avoid last-minute braking or lane drift.

question: While driving in a construction zone, you should:
options: a:Expect the unexpected.,b:Slightly increase your speed to pass quickly.,c:Expect workers to yield to motorists.
note: Construction zones present unusual hazards and changing conditions; drive with extra caution and be ready for slowed traffic or workers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is NOT a safe practice on the interstate?
options: a:Changing lanes without signaling.,b:Slower traffic keeping to the right.,c:If you miss your exit, proceeding to the next exit.
note: Always signal lane changes on interstates; failing to signal is unsafe and illegal despite other correct practices like keeping right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking, how far from the curb should your wheels be?
options: a:Within one foot of the curb.,b:Within two feet of the curb.,c:Within three feet of the curb.,d:Directly on the curb for stability.
note: When parallel parking, position your wheels parallel and within one foot of the curb so you do not obstruct traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you always drive slower than the surrounding traffic?
options: a:No — driving excessively slow can block traffic and be dangerous.,b:Yes — always safer to drive slower than others.,c:Yes — it is a good defensive driving technique to drive well under the flow of traffic.
note: While you should slow for hazards or poor conditions, driving too slowly and obstructing normal traffic flow can be unsafe and subject to citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what speed should you travel?
options: a:At the speed limit regardless of conditions.,b:At the same speed as surrounding vehicles.,c:At a speed appropriate for the road and weather conditions.
note: Drive at or below the posted speed limit and always slow down when road or weather conditions make normal speeds unsafe.

question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted only from the side next to the dashed line.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted from both directions.
note: Only traffic on the side with the dashed line may cross to pass; traffic on the solid-line side may not pass.

question: Driving defensively includes which of the following actions?
options: a:Keeping your eyes moving to scan for hazards.,b:Focusing only on the vehicle directly in front of you.,c:Leaving a fixed stare down the road.
note: Defensive driving requires scanning the road and surroundings continuously, not staring at one point or only at the car ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, to whom must you yield?
options: a:You must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic must yield to you.,c:Pedestrians must yield to left-turning vehicles.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight and to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what is the safest response?
options: a:Get out of their way.,b:Challenge them.,c:Speed up to get away.,d:Follow closely to report them.
note: Avoid engaging or escalating; safely yield or move away to reduce the chance of conflict or collision.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility, what should you do to improve your visibility to others?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Turn on parking lights only.,c:Use emergency flashers only.,d:Stop immediately in the roadway.
note: Use headlights whenever conditions make it hard to see other vehicles so others can also see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you make a left turn when turning from a one-way street?
options: a:From the lane nearest the left curb.,b:From the lane nearest the center of the street.,c:From the lane nearest the right curb.,d:From any lane as long as you signal.
note: Turn from the lane closest to the direction you intend to go; on a one-way street making a left, use the lane nearest the left curb and enter the first legal lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When traffic is merging into your freeway lane, what should you do?
options: a:Make room for the merging traffic if you can do so safely.,b:Assert your right-of-way by accelerating.,c:Always maintain your lane position and speed.,d:Brake hard to force them to stop.
note: If traffic conditions permit, adjust speed or change lanes to safely allow merging vehicles to enter.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle moving in the same direction, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After about three seconds.,c:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,d:When you are one car length ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Only return to your original lane when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror; also check blind spots before moving back into the lane.

question: Why should you use headlights during rain, snow, or fog?
options: a:So other drivers can see your vehicle.,b:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,c:To keep your engine warm.
note: Headlights make your vehicle more visible to others in poor weather; in South Dakota, use low beams when windshield wipers are on.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:At all times to avoid striking them, regardless of the situation.,b:Only if they are inside a marked crosswalk.,c:Only when traffic signals favor the pedestrian.,d:Only when they wave you across.
note: Always do everything possible to avoid hitting pedestrians, giving them the right-of-way whenever necessary.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you do?
options: a:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass (give the motorcycle a full lane).,b:Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder.,c:Stay in the right lane as much as possible and share a lane with the motorcycle.,d:Pass very closely to reduce wind effects.
note: Give motorcycles a full lane when passing; never share a lane or crowd the rider.

question: If a green light changes to yellow while you are already in the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection.,c:Accelerate to exit quicker.
note: If you're already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, proceed and clear it safely rather than stopping mid-intersection.

question: What is the only proven method to remove alcohol from your system?
options: a:Allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol.,b:Drink strong coffee to sober up.,c:Take a cold shower.,d:Exercise vigorously to sweat it out.
note: Only time lets the body eliminate alcohol. Coffee, showers, and exercise do not reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

question: A broken yellow centerline indicates:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,d:You must stay in your lane at all times.
note: A broken yellow line permits crossing the centerline to pass when no oncoming traffic is present and it is safe.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, what is the correct action?
options: a:Turn around and find another route; do not drive through flooded areas.,b:Slam on the brakes and cross quickly.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway.
note: Never drive through floodwater; even shallow water can hide hazards or sweep your vehicle away—find an alternate route.

question: Which lights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog; high beams reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: Which lights should you use as daylight fades to make your vehicle more visible?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Emergency flashers.,d:High beam headlights.
note: Turn on low beam headlights as daylight fades so others can see your vehicle; high beams are for open, unlit roads with no nearby traffic.

question: When changing lanes, which action is prohibited?
options: a:Attempting to pass or change lanes within an intersection.,b:Checking blind spots by looking over your shoulder.,c:Signaling before initiating the lane change.,d:Checking for vehicles already in the lane you want to enter.
note: Never change lanes or pass within an intersection; always check mirrors, blind spots, and signal before moving laterally.

question: When used on roadways, bicycles are legally considered:
options: a:Hazards.,b:Vehicles.,c:Dangerous objects.
note: Bicycles are treated as vehicles on the road; bicyclists and motorists must follow the same traffic laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Swinging too wide into another lane.,b:Signaling to alert other drivers.,c:Slowing down before the turn.,d:Checking for pedestrians.
note: Do not swing wide when turning; this can cut across adjacent lanes and endanger other road users.

question: Yellow centerlines on the roadway separate:
options: a:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:All carpool lanes from regular lanes.,d:Bicycle lanes from traffic lanes.
note: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way roadway and separate traffic traveling in opposite directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a driver view right-of-way rules while driving?
options: a:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way to avoid collisions.,b:Assume all drivers will obey right-of-way rules exactly.,c:Assume most drivers obey the rules so you needn't worry.
note: Even with right-of-way rules, be prepared to yield when necessary to prevent crashes because other drivers may not follow the rules.

question: When parking next to a curb, when should you signal?
options: a:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to the curb.
note: Signal whenever you are moving to or from the curb to alert other drivers and pedestrians of your intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: May you drive off the traveled roadway onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If there are two or more lanes in your direction.
note: You may not pass by driving off the paved or main-traveled portion of the roadway onto the shoulder.

question: In bad weather, what driving technique is recommended?
options: a:Steer and brake smoothly.,b:Steer off the road at the first sign of trouble.,c:Brake hard to stop quickly.,d:Drive in a low gear at all times.
note: Control the vehicle with smooth steering and gentle braking to reduce the chance of losing traction in adverse weather.

question: Which of the following is true about crosswalks?
options: a:They may be either marked with paint or unmarked and both are legal crosswalks.,b:They are always indicated by pavement markings.,c:They are always unmarked.
note: Crosswalks exist whether they are painted or not; drivers must stop behind crosswalks to allow pedestrians to cross.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels away from the curb.,b:Turn the wheels toward the curb.,c:Keep the front wheels straight.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if the brakes fail.

question: How does driver fatigue affect your crash risk?
options: a:Increase errors in speed and distance judgment.,b:Cause you to fall asleep at the wheel and crash.,c:Help you make faster decisions.,d:Only lead to minor delays.
note: Fatigue impairs judgment of speed and distance, slows decision-making, and can cause you to fall asleep behind the wheel, greatly increasing crash risk.

question: Reaction time is slower after which activity?
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping well.,c:Working hard at a job.,d:Exercising regularly.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes and reaction time, impairing vision, alertness, and judgment — all important for safe driving.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicate for drivers turning in that direction?
options: a:Prepare to stop and yield; the green arrow protection is ending.,b:Speed up to complete your turn before it changes.,c:You do not need to signal when turning.,d:You must stop immediately and remain stopped.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the green turn arrow is ending; be prepared to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what is the correct way to re-enter the roadway?
options: a:Slow down, check traffic, and when safe gradually steer back onto the roadway.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Stop and wait for help.
note: Do not jerk the wheel; reduce speed, check for traffic, and carefully steer back onto the pavement when it's safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Facing a green light with pedestrians in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Proceed because you have the green light.,c:Honk to let pedestrians know to clear the crosswalk.,d:Speed through before pedestrians finish crossing.
note: Even on green, yield to pedestrians already in the intersection; drivers must yield when turning on a steady green.

question: If you've had several beers, what actually reduces the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Waiting several hours for the body to metabolize it.,b:Taking a cold shower.,c:Drinking several cups of coffee.
note: Only time will reduce alcohol concentration; cold showers or coffee do not speed alcohol elimination from your system.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure for making a right turn?
options: a:Signal, slow, and approach from the lane nearest the right curb before turning.,b:Signal, slow, and get into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.,c:Approach in the lane nearest the curb then move toward the middle before turning.
note: Signal in advance, slow, and make the turn from the lane nearest the right curb, staying close to the curb as practical.

question: Alcohol acts as which type of substance on the body?
options: a:A depressant that slows bodily and nervous system functions.,b:A stimulant that increases alertness.,c:Neither a stimulant nor a depressant.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant that lowers reaction time and judgment even at low concentrations.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,b:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,c:They brake more slowly than cars.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly; following too closely reduces your ability to avoid a sudden stop and may cause a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do stopping distances and collision severity change with vehicle speed?
options: a:Both increase as vehicle speed increases.,b:They decrease as speed increases.,c:They are unaffected by speed.
note: As speed increases, stopping distance and the force of impact increase, elevating collision severity and injury risk.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or holding a white cane, you should:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to them.,b:Expect them to yield to you.,c:Honk to let them know you are there.
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians using a guide dog or cane have the right-of-way; yield and proceed only when safe.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Both alertness and coordination are impaired.,b:Only alertness is affected.,c:Only coordination is affected.,d:None of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs reduce alertness, coordination, reaction time, and concentration — all critical for safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you follow the directions of a school crossing guard?
options: a:At all times while they are directing traffic.,b:Only during school hours, not during evenings.,c:Only if there are children present.,d:Only if police are also present.
note: Drivers must always obey instructions from school crossing guards to ensure student safety near schools.

question: How should you apply the gas pedal for safe acceleration?
options: a:Press it slowly and smoothly.,b:Tap it lightly in short bursts.,c:Depress it quickly to get moving fast.
note: Accelerate gradually and smoothly; sudden acceleration can cause wheelspin and loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.,b:Yield only to vehicles coming from your right.,c:Always slow down but never stop.
note: Slow or stop if necessary and give the right-of-way to crossing or merging vehicles close enough to cause a conflict.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Whenever it helps prevent a collision.,b:Never; always use your legal right-of-way.,c:Often, even at controlled intersections.,d:Only when a police officer tells you to.
note: Yielding your right-of-way to avoid a crash is appropriate; never assume others will yield to you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Pedestrians and oncoming vehicles with the right-of-way.,b:Only vehicles turning right.,c:Only vehicles approaching from the left.,d:No one; left turns have priority.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians who have the right-of-way before completing your turn.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:At all times when pedestrians are in the crosswalk.,b:Only if the pedestrians first wave the driver on.,c:Only if pedestrians are not distracted by devices.,d:Only when traffic lights indicate a walk signal.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians already in a crosswalk, stopping completely if necessary.

question: When a school bus is stopped ahead to load or unload children with lights flashing, what must drivers do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Change lanes and pass the bus cautiously.,c:Come to a complete stop until all the children have left the bus.,d:Slow down to 10 mph and proceed.
note: Stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights and its stop arm is extended; do not proceed until the lights are off and the arm is retracted.

question: Alcohol acts as which type of substance on the central nervous system?
options: a:A depressant.,b:A stimulant.,c:An antihistamine.,d:A hallucinogen.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain function, impairs judgment, and reduces coordination and reaction time.

question: If parking facing uphill where there is no curb, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels toward the edge of the road (right).,b:Turn the wheels away from the edge of the road.,c:Keep the wheels straight ahead.
note: When parked uphill without a curb, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle will roll off the roadway, not into traffic, if brakes fail.

question: What actually removes alcohol from your body?
options: a:Take a cold shower.,b:Wait; only time removes alcohol from the body.,c:Drink strong coffee.,d:Do vigorous exercise to sober up.
note: Only time eliminates alcohol from your system; eating, coffee, showers, or exercise do not speed up alcohol metabolism.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about vehicle blind spots is correct?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:Blind spots are eliminated by having one outside mirror on each side.,c:Blind spots can be fully seen using only the rearview mirrors.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars, so avoid lingering beside them.

question: What should you do to help prevent hydroplaning on wet pavement?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Use cruise control to keep constant speed.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it begins to rain.,d:Increase tire pressure immediately.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by excessive speed on wet roads; reduce speed to maintain tire contact with the pavement.

question: If a truck or bus is turning right and you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn before you turn.,b:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.,c:Turn quickly ahead of the truck or bus.
note: Large vehicles may swing wide when turning; do not try to pass between them and the curb—wait until they finish their turn.

question: What must you do when a traffic signal displays a steady red arrow?
options: a:Drivers may turn in the arrow's direction after making a complete stop.,b:Traffic in the indicated lane must remain stopped and may not proceed in that direction.,c:Drivers may turn in the arrow’s direction immediately.,d:Drivers may turn if no other traffic is present.
note: A steady red arrow prohibits movement in the arrow's direction; drivers must wait for a green signal to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two lanes are moving in the same direction and you are in the left lane while others pass on the right, what should you do if someone behind wants to go faster?
options: a:Move into the right lane when it is safe to do so.,b:Stay in the left lane to avoid impeding traffic.,c:Drive onto the shoulder briefly to let them pass.,d:Brake sharply to signal them to pass.
note: If you're in the left lane and traffic is passing on the right, move into the right lane when safe to allow faster drivers to pass.
